notes.title: Station Haven 3 - Development Update 001
notes.content:
Long time no see!
Hello everyone! It's been a while since the last post. 

I do want to apologize for the silence. Last few months have been a little more tough and so my focused was shifted a little more towards personal priorities. This did not mean that I have stopped working on the game altogether, but just that the progress was slowed down.



It's a little more difficult to create posts like these on a more regular basis, but what I do use more often is my own personal discord server to talk more regularly. So, if you'd like more regular updates, feel free to join at the following link: https://discord.gg/bJZCtEp

For the future, I will try and post an update at least once every-other week.
(This does not include the Discord updates)




Steam Next Fest!
Station Haven 3's Demo was available in the last Steam Next Fest! Being able to find my own game and seeing other people finding it on Steam's front page has been one huge achievement! Thank you to all who have found the game on Steam's Next Fest and have decided to either play it or wish listed!

Through Steam Next Fest, we have basically more than doubled the number of wish lists! Additionally, around 20% of the people who have played the Demo have also wish listed the game! I am unsure how good stats like these are, but to me, that's absolutely crazy.




If you are one of the people that played the Demo & wish listed, please join my discord or message me directly! I would love to hear your opinion and feedback of the Demo or to listen to any kind of criticism you might have for the game! Any feedback, to me, is good feedback.





Now, it's time to go over some
TeasersLet's finally go over some of the stuff that's been removed, what's has been done and what's there in the future to come:

What's been removed: 
As I mentioned previously, my vision for the full game release is to have a completely separate instance compared to the demo. What I mean by this is that the only things that will really be familiar if you play both the Demo and the Full game will be: the universe, some of the core gameplay mechanics and the story plot ( I hope you paid attention ;) ). 



And so, the following has been removed (or reworked):

All cassettes

All "event trigger" locations (if you were grinding for the "That's just my luck" achievement, you know exactly what I am talking about) and their respective event.

All repair locations & repair system.

A lot of assets.

The Manual (⚰️)

Some other things that I'll keep secret for now.

I won't tell you exactly what's been removed or reworked (other than the Manual - that thing has been thrown out into space) so I can keep things a little interesting.




What's been updated (with GIFs!):
Here we will go on both gameplay mechanics, but will also dig a tiny bit into the technical side for those that might be intrigued by that


Gameplay:
All of these are still a "Work-In-Progress". The following may or may not be different in the final game.

New Item Interaction

The player can now pick up random items and carry them around

The items can be taken for a spin by holding down a key and then moving the mouse

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45350516/75825a8a5be41e3842a192b0344b7d31bc2a59b4.gif"]

New Item Delivery Mechanic (Some of you might see where this might be going already)

Some items are important and need to be brought somewhere to trigger certain interactions. 

Only the correct item will work! Make sure it fits.

(I could have probably used a different second item to show what works and what doesn't)

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45350516/9efb7683829da381f9e500edbec2480246c0d473.gif"]

New Inventory System

An easy way to track all the items you have collected throughout the game.

This inventory system will be persistent throughout the game.

The inventory is broken down in 3 sections: Cassettes (they are back), Important and Notes.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45350516/1bd077326387a4ab2863a1b561a4e98f42c4f0c6.gif"]

Inventory System Interaction

With the Inventory available, you can now pick up these items and have that be shown in your inventory.

When picked up, the item will be shown in its designated spot

This design is intentional and will have its use.

You can click on any items that you have to get a short description for it at the bottom (despite the low-quality gif, it's there).

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45350516/11e7494f7b10388d5b4e22183214e2e11ebf7e88.gif"]

Better movement

Added jumping

Added crouching

Better walking & sprinting animations

Sounds will now be different depending on the surface of the floor underneath the player.

Save & Load Game systems

Long awaited as it was not present in the Demo and a lot of people have voiced their frustration over that. I did not create a full save system for the Demo as I deemed it to be "too short to matter". This was a mistake on my part

Of course, the full game shall be present with a full and working Save / Load Game system.


Technical stuff:
Updated engine: [strike]Unreal Engine 5.4[/strike] Unreal Engine 5.6. This update was done for the following reasons:

Better Lumen lighting optimizations.

Metahumans.

Better animations.

Overall better performance.

Completely removed level dependencies:

When this project first started, the scope of it was much way smaller. Because of that, I have made a lot of beginner mistakes. Once the scope of the game became bigger, a lot of these issues resurfaced, and a lot of reworking was done for it.

Optimizations for a lot of redundant stuff and a much better optimization focused on running things more smoothly.


The story:
Yes, you have read that right. As time has passed, my view of the story has also become different.



Does that mean that the story presented in the Demo is now non-cannon?

Quite the contrary. The story in the Demo is still as I want it to be, and I am glad to have that out there.

At the Demo's release, I already had the entire plot and story written down.

Now? That story has become barely a 15% in a much, much, bigger story.


What's next?
Well, simply put, more development! But also, more communication. I will try from now on to keep you guys updated on the development of the game and where we are.

The focus in these last few months has been basically on the actual core mechanics of the game and the skeleton that will support everything. So, currently, there's no real "Game" yet available.



Further updates will go into displaying more gameplay updates, but we will slowly start going into environments and perhaps even something else.



And, if you read this far, we can also let you into a little secret:

A trailer is coming soon.


Thank you for reading this far!
That's it for today! Hope you guys had a good read. 

Once again, I would be glad to have you in my discord server at the link above or at the Discord button below. I post more updates there.



Until next time!

notes.title: Demo Update - Patch 0.2.2 - Final Update
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
Long time no see! I hope everyone has been doing well. I want to firstly apologize for the radio silence for the last, almost, 2 months. I have been getting over a burnout and had some difficult times in my personal life lately.
I was finally able to get back into the game thanks to a player that has recently joined the server (discord link below) to ask for some achievement tips. Due to this, I was actually able to get back into finishing the last update for the game!

Now, without further ado:

Patch 0.2.2 - The Final Demo Update

Fixed bugs:

 Fixed a bug where the "TAB" button wouldn’t work after switching pages once in the manual.
 Fixed a bug where some assets were slightly misplaced or missing some important textures
 Fixed the "headlight" the player has so that it now won't clip out of existence if the player backs up too much into a wall. Also adjusted the light on it to reach slightly further.
 Fixed a bug where the player couldn't finish the game. (Crazy)
 Fixed a bug where some assets were visible when they shouldn't be.
 Fixed a bug where there could be two instances of the "Pause" menu active at the same time.
 Fixed some bugs in the Options menu where the Sensitivity would not save after clicking "Apply". Now, sensitivity will stay constant after pressing Apply and will remain constant even after game restarts.
 Fixed "1977" (hopefully).


Adjustments:

 Adjusted some cassettes to appear more often
 Adjusted some events to have a higher chance of triggering (This one's for you, achievement hunters)


Quality of Life:

 Added a few new assets.
 Updated the map to follow up on player feedback. Now, the map will look more "static". This change was made after seeing that many players thought that map was digital and not static. Also updated the position of the map itself.
 Added SPRINTING as a response to player feedback. Press "SHIFT" to ever-so-slightly increase your movement speed. Just don't be too loud, mkay? ;)
NOTE: Sprinting was not originally designed to exist in this game, so be careful that you don't soft-lock yourself.
 Removed the option to change the sensitivity from the "Start" Level. The way I spaghetti coded this made it so this is not achievable. (Sorry)
 Optimizations to some existing logics to improve performance.


Note:
The "reset" of the game when changing the settings in the Start Level is still present and will remain. This is due to my faulty design of the menu. This kind of menu will not be in the final game, but unfortunately it will remain in the Demo.

And that is it... for now
This will the last and final, major update for Station Haven 3's demo. From now on, the focus and all the work shall be going towards the actual full game.
I want to thank each and every one of you that has played the Demo, given feedback for the game or has even looked upon this little project of mine. Your support really does mean a lot and helps push me forward.

Updates stop..but only on Steam Announcements
I will be going slightly more silent on Steam from now on to focus on working towards the final game. However, that doesn't mean I will be going completely dark. I will be posting decently regular updates on my discord server along with, at times, doing some stream on twitch. So, feel free to click the link to access my discord server and join the server to keep up with news.

Happy Easter Holidays for those who are celebrating!
I wish all of you happy holidays for the upcoming Easter holidays! I hope you guys have the time you wish to have and get to relax!

Thank you once more for all the support!
See you aboard Station Haven 3!

notes.title: Patch 0.2.1 - The Lore Update
notes.content:
Hello all! I hope you have been enjoying the 0.2 patch and have been unlocking them achievements.

After listening to a lot more player feedback, I have went ahead and prepared a new patch for you all! The lore update.

This update aims to give you guys more information about the story of the game, explain gameplay elements even more and give you all a better teaser for the Final game!

I hope you guys enjoy!

Official Patch Notes - Version 0.2.1 

Bugfixes:
 - Fixed some instances where the player could get stuck
 - Adjusted some assets to fit the universe a bit better

New:
 - Terminal update: the "VIEW" command is now available and usable for the Demo. Go out there and find out what mysteries it hides.

notes.title: Demo Update - Official Patch Notes - Version 0.2.0
notes.content:
Hello everybody!

I'm glad to have you all here. I am glad to present to you the official patch notes for version 0.2.0 for the Demo!
This will very likely be the final major implementation of the Demo (excluding bug fixes). From now on, the future of the full game, Station Haven 3, shall be slowly built onto the final game.

I really hope you guys have enjoyed the game!
If you'd like to leave some feedback, feel free to join the discord to chat!

Without further ado..

Official Patch 0.2.0

What's new:

Added Achievements. There's a total of 6 (4 hidden).
Added new "Random Events".
Added Station "responses" to certain Critical Module states. An example can be found in the Manual, but there are more.
New secret [REDACTED] added


Bugfixes: (All bugfixes will be marked as spoilers, so only look through them if you have played the game)[spoiler]
-Fixed a bug where, after the player would finish a Loop, the "Pod" door would have missing textures.
-Fixed some places where players could get stuck.
-Fixed some typos in the Manual.
-Fixed the Credits end page where it was ever so slightly blue
-Fixed some assets with missing collision boxes.
-Fixed a bug where the player would be able to move while using the Terminal
-Fixed a bug where, if the player would ALT+TAB while using the Terminal, the game would break.[/spoiler]

Possibly fixed:

Fixed an issue where, if a player starts the game for the first time, opening the "Settings Menu" will show the "Graphics Quality" to be at nothing.


Quality of Life (QoL):

Added a "Controls" page into the Manual.
Added a 60 FPS limit. Currently, this does not save between restarts.
Added a counter to the objectives for how many Cassettes the player has collected and how many are left.
Added a "small headlight", so the player can see around their immediate head area in dark spots.
Added a counter to the STATUS ALL check. Now, after the Terminal analysis, it will say how many issues out of how many total there are. (Previously, it will only say how many issues were found)
Lowered the Motion Blur to an acceptable level. Option menu for this is not yet available. 
Updated the Terminal to now properly present whether a door is opening or closing. Instead of just saying "Triggering…", it will now say "Opening…" or "Closing…" depending on the action.
Updated the "Random Event" system. Now, ALL events have a higher chance of happening.


Currently known bugs:

One small instance where the Life Support & Generator Display will remain red even when the Status of both sections is good.
The possibility of getting stuck behind doors and breaking the game.
Possibility of the graphics bug still lingering there somewhere, somehow. If you find yourself having no Graphic Settings at the beginning of the game, press any of the arrow buttons to fix it.

notes.title: Demo is now available!
notes.content:
Station Haven 3 Demo - Officially out
Hello everyone!

I am very glad to welcome you all to the official release of the Demo for Station Haven 3.

The future of the Demo

This will be marked as Patch 0.1.1.
We had an initial closed release for the Demo where I was able to find a good amount of bugs. I was able to fix pretty much all of them while waiting for Steam's review to be completed.

The game is still not yet perfect and there are still a few more things to add. More QoL updates will be coming along with Achievements, but the main game itself and the story I wanted to present for the Demo are here and I wanted to share them with you.

The differences between the Demo and the Full Game
The story that you will be experiencing throughout the Demo is unique to the Demo. A teaser for the world I am building so to speak.
The premise and the actions you will do are part of the final game as well, along with the majority of the main gameplay mechanics present in the game.

However, everything that is related to the story that is in the Demo will remain in the Demo. This means that, when the full game comes out, a new entire story will be available with the initial presented premise.

Welcome aboard Station Haven 3!

I am looking forward to your feedback and I am curious to see what you will think of the game. 
Any kind of feedback is welcomed!

Enjoy!

notes.title: Demo official release date announcement
notes.content:
Long time no see!
Hello everyone! Long time no see!
I would like to start off by apologizing for the radio silence. I was planning on doing weekly updates on development, but there has been quite a few things happening lately. 

Accidentally deleting the entire map losing 1 month of progress.
Yup. I have, in all my glory, deleted the entire map by accident. Permanently.
This has happened in a random Saturday, 2-3 weeks ago, where I encountered a very weird, but persistent bug, where, after adjusting some lights, my Player Character lost all of it's collisions. I have wasted 10+ hours trying to fix it, and by the end I gave up on fixing it.
As I am a programmer, I always have backups. So, of course, I decided at the end of the day that it would be better for me to just "re-add" my player character from my back-up archives.

My most recent back-up was 1 month old. (Notice how I never said I was a "good" programmer)
I replaced my character, but only partially, and this proved to not work.
This then has lead to my biggest mistake. You see, for some reason, my map was placed in the exact same folder as the player character and, in my frustration and defeat, I have deleted the entire folder. With Shift Delete...
Upon re-opening Unreal Engine.... I could easily feel any kind of color draining from my face when all I had open was... nothing.

Luckily, it was not a big loss, as the difference between the map at the time and from the backup were not THAT big, as the majority of the work during that month was done in modules created by me & worked by me.

Emotionally however... I have been doing back-ups every day since then.. Lesson learned I guess...
Now, let's back to our business

Demo Release Date
We are fast approaching the day where I will finally be able to release the Demo with all of you.
It has been a very long journey for me, one that is I would say, only half way done.

Initially, I planned for the Demo to release from the 23rd of January until the 6th of February. Well, this was slightly delayed due to my silliness, but, if all goes to plan and no other major bugs/deletions happen, the official release date for the demo is: 

10th of February
Mark your calendars.

What to expect from Station Haven 3 - Demo
I want to go into details into a few things in relation to the game prior to the release, and more specifically, I want to go into what exactly this Demo is supposed to be and is supposed to achieve.

With this Demo, I want to test the following:

 The gameplay mechanics
 The immersion of the players
 The immersion of the story


The "main gameplay interaction element" is not fully done and won't be done for the Demo.
This is done because I want to first get some feedback from you guys and to see what you guys think about it and how you feel.
Spoiler version:
[expand type=spoiler expanded=false]The main gameplay mechanic is Fixing the Station, where you will, as of now, hold E to fix a certain area of the Station. This is represented by a simple progress bar.[/expand]

I believe that, ironically, the gameplay element is the weakest part of my game at the moment. Making games that are engaging is harder than you think!
However, for the other elements of the game, I believe they are pretty good and I hope you guys will enjoy them!

And that is all
This will not be that last 0.X update, but, other than bug fixes, there won't be any other updates to the Demo. The Demo shall be a "separate" story of the final game, so treat it as only a little treat of what's to come.

I hope you guys will enjoy the demo when it will come out, and I also hope that you won't find any bugs.

See you aboard the Station!

notes.title: 12th of January Update & How the progress is going for the Demo
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Hope everybody had a good week! I know a lot of you will be going back to work (if you haven't already) from tomorrow, so I wish you guys to have a good and prosperous year! May thy work hours feel short and paycheck get bigger.

Let's pick up from where we left off last week with a small announcement!

41 Wishlist's! Thank you!
It's crazy for me, but we have actually managed to reach 41 wishlists on Steam with little to no marketing! I have 0 clue on how's that happened, but my god am I grateful for that. Thanks to all of you who are wishlisting the game! It means a lot!

This does lead me into the following topic, which is:

Trailer for Station Haven 3
A trailer is also currently in the works for the game. It will also present short "mechanics" of the game, but it will be mainly focused on the narrative part of the story and the mystery of the game. There's no release date on it yet, but do stay tuned for it as it will be coming soon.

The current status of development
As of the 12th of January, 2025.

 Tutorial refined and added more "hints/leads" for the player to better understand where to go, what to do and how to do it (Thank you Wife for playtesting)
 70% of voice acting added (50% last week)
 Main gameplay and narrative objects added, but not entirely yet (I'd say it's at like 30% done, but should be done by next week)


However, there is one thing I did discover this week, and that is:
The size of the Demo (And the optimization of it)
Upon my latest Test Shipping Build (game devs out there, always do this every now and then to make sure there's no problems), I have noticed that some of the assets I am using are quite.. well, large.
Now, this was to be expected to some extent, because I am using Unreal Engine 5.4 and I am using quite realistic (if not hyper realistic) assets. However, I am not pleased with the fact that the game is currently 14 GB big. On the latest poll I did on Discord (Which you should join, link down below), people seemed to not have an issue with the size, but I still find it quite large. I will be attempting to lower this size for the Demo at the very least, but do know that if I do fail, this might be the final size of the Demo...

Demo release date
Currently, there are no delays happening, so the initial start date of 23rd of January is still holding strong. I should be able to, from that day, release the demo in the next 2 weeks.
Majority of important things are in place, and the game is becoming more and more of an actual game with every day, so stay tuned for that.

Thank you!
Once again, thank you! Whether you read through this whole thing, skimmed through it or skipped to the end, you even knowing this post exists is making me more and more confident to keep working and bring you the world I envision.
I truly hope to bring this game to life in the demo and hook you guys in the world I created. And we're very close to that date now!

I hope you guys will have a nice week! See you next Sunday with another update (and maybe more ;) )

notes.title: Happy New Year! Current development updates & Potential Delay
notes.content:
Happy New Year!
Happy 2025 everybody! Hope everyone was able to have a calm/relaxing/fun new year celebration! I wish all of you an amazing 2025! I hope you all will be able to achieve what you want for 2025.
As for me, this year will be quite an interesting year at the very least, as I will finally be able to achieve a life long dream of mine, and that is to make a game.

Speaking of
The current status of Development
As of 4th of January, 2025.
I will rather currently go into details that are related to the Demo, as they are the more "pressing" ones. Currently, a game is playable already. However, there is not much of an ambiance, hook and much of a story just yet (that's implemented). To go into more detail as to what was completed since last week:

 Tutorial
 50% of voice acting added to the game and already implemented. One of the actors is already fully into the game.
 A start for a narrative for the player

The game is technically now playable (but no point at which credits roll), but there's still a lot to add to polish a better ambiance and to make every player's experience more unique and each playthrough more different.

If the game is already playable, why not release the Demo?
Great question, voice in my head. Well, it's mainly because I want to use this Demo for a multitude of reasons:

 See how the game mechanics are received
 Analyze performance on other machines (higher and lower ones)
 Get more feedback on the story elements of the game.

Of course, a lot of stuff will still be quite unpolished for the Demo, but I believe it's better to catch issues like these early on before they become too engrained into the fundamentals.

As for the Demo, the current projection still stands from the 23rd of January... however..

Potential for delay
To keep everything transparent, there is a potential for a delay due to some personal professional issues. My job has unfortunately been affected by the global layoffs and I am currently still looking for one. The delay itself can be caused for some interviews that I might have to take which can take who knows how many days at times and will slow down my progress. I hope you understand that, as of now, a job will be my priority over working on Haven 3. Perhaps in the future that won't be the case and my job will be to make these games, but that day is not today.

On the plus side, I am now finally (after many months) able to rest and work more on Station Haven 3.
On the obvious negative side.. no job = no income.
And before anyone asks, I don't intend to make a funding page at the current time. I have a good amount of money saved up and should be fine. I also have a good amount of faith in myself to find something soon, but I do feel like you guys should know about the potential delay.

Thank you!
Once again, thank you for reading through, skimming through this post or skipping at the bottom. You acknowledging this post is more than enough for me.

See you next week! In the meantime, feel free to join the Discord. I post more regular stuff there.

notes.title: First Regular Update & Thank you for Wish listings & Pricing
notes.content:
Before we begin
Happy holidays and a happy new year to everyone! So sorry that it took so long to post a first update here, I am still somewhat new to this.
Expect such updates to be more regular. Currently aiming to have 1 at least once a week.

A formal introduction
Hello everybody!

I feel like a formal introduction is due.
My name is Denis. I am a 25 year old software engineer born and still living in Romania. I have been working as a software engineer for ~4.5 years now, mainly in the embedded field (With a little bit of CPP).

I decided to take a dive into game development quite a long while ago. I had some initial projects that I started, fewer that I managed to work further, but only this one I was able to bring this far, and soon fully bring out to all of you.

Currently, I am the sole developer for this game. It is being created in Unreal Engine 5.4.

What is Station Haven 3 and how it begun

Station Haven 3 will be my first officially released game. A story driven game where you will uncover the truth about the Haven 3 Station.
Without going into any other details that could potentially spoil anything, the game itself is something that I came up with over the course of a few days! It will be a story that will try and create a "what if" scenario, based on accurate real data and historic events that have happened in the future. Some of the current screenshots on the Steam Page actually have some hidden details ;).

The current status of Development & future projections.
As of the 29th of December, 2024.
Currently, the fundamentals of the game have been finished for a few weeks now. Again, I cannot say too much due to spoilers as some of the mechanics are tied to the story & gameplay, but some of the details I can give are:

 Main important mechanics of the game. Polishing & details, but that's forever ongoing as it can always be better.
 Tutorial & Ways to teach the player how to play the game
 Optimizations & bug fixes & fail safes to make sure the player does not accidentally "escape" (from Haven). I am still confident someone WILL somehow manage to do so, so take it as a challenge.
 Hiring & Collaborating with Voice Actors. The voice actor for the Demo has already finished their job, so expect to hear a friendly and lovely voice very soon.
 The premise of the story, the story itself and the endings


Future projections
The future projections are, of course, to finish the game. Obviously. However, to go into more detail:

 Asset optimizations & Options Menu.
 Bug fixes of the bugs I know and those I don't (I fear the latter more).
 Polishing of the game mechanics and implementing the story I wrote into the game itself.
 The release of a Demo in the near future (January, at worst February) then seeing the game through to it's completion.


The Price of the game: 3$ (three dollars)
I don't wish to start an entire paragraph here where I will mention the price somewhere randomly in the middle. So, 3$ (three dollars).
This potentially can be subject to change, but I will NEVER go above 5$ (five dollars). I feel like, currently, for this being my first ever published game & you guys putting trust in me, the price is fair. I am already in a way bigger negative financially ever since I started working on this game (Hiring of Voice Actors & Asset purchases etc.) and making money was never really a goal with this game, but selling it for a price instead of making it free will also help me financially to recoup.

Demo release date: January (Hopefully)
Initially, when I started work on this game (~28th of October), the plan was to release a demo somewhere in the middle of December. Well, that boat sailed, did a trip around the world twice and then retired. It was an easy underestimation on my part & I underestimated how little work I'd be working during Christmas/Holiday period.
However, a first demo is very very feasible to be released towards the end of January, at worst the beginning of February. So, a window between the following dates:
Between the 23rd of January until the 7th of February, the Demo should come out if all goes to plan.

Thank you!
Thank you for reading through this! Whether you read the whole thing, skimmed through it or skipped to the end, you even acknowledging this post gives me more drive to keep working on the game.
I truly hope you guys will believe in me going in further. Making a game has forever been a dream of mine, and knowing that I am closer than ever to do.. honestly? Makes me very nervous...
But we keep going.

This was also my first ever official Announcement on Steam like.. ever. So I am unsure if there's any kind of rules or etiquettes I have to follow

Until then, happy holidays and happy new year to everyone! I hope to see you guys soon aboard Station Haven 3.
